search.heading: 4.3.1 Temperature thresholds
search.snippet: Cold Chain Product categories must be stored, handled and transported within Table 4.1. These thresholds apply unless the customer contract, product licence or Quality-approved lane validation requires stricter limits. Table 4.1 — Cold Chain Temperature Thresholds |Product category|Required temperature range|Maximum excursion time|Escalation action| |---|---|---|---| |Category A — frozen biologics|-25°C to -15°C|15 minutes|Immediate Quarantine; Quality call within 1 hour| |Category B — chilled pharmaceuticals|+2°C to +8°C|30 minutes|Quarantine; deviation opened within 2 hours| |Category C — clinical trial kits|+2°C to +8°C|20 minutes|Quarantine; sponsor notified within 4 hours| |Category D — fresh premium food|0°C to +4°C|45 minutes|Site review; customer notice within 8 hours if released stock affected| |Category E — controlled ambient medicines|+15°C to +25°C|120 minutes|Quality review within 24 hours| |Category F — chocolate and confectionery|+12°C to +18°C|180 minutes|Operations review; hold if visible bloom or melt risk| |Category G — temperature-sensitive electronics|+5°C to +30°C|240 minutes|Engineering review if condensation observed| |Category H — cosmetics with stability limits|+10°C to +25°C|180 minutes|Customer approval before dispatch if excursion repeated| For temperature excursion procedures, see Section 4.3.2. For incident classification, see Section 3.1 and Appendix B.

search.heading: 4.3.4 Temperature monitoring
search.snippet: All cold rooms must have continuous calibrated monitoring. Alarm set points must be tighter than product limits by at least 1°C for chilled and ambient categories and 2°C for frozen categories. Manual checks must be performed at least twice per shift where automated monitoring is active and hourly where automated monitoring is unavailable. If automated monitoring fails, then manual checks must begin within 30 minutes — except when a validated backup logger is active, visible and configured to alert Quality.

search.heading: 4.3.3 Cold chain loading
search.snippet: Cold chain vehicles must be pre-cooled before loading. Required pre-cooling duration is: 1. Frozen vehicles: minimum 45 minutes. 2. Chilled vehicles: minimum 30 minutes. 3. Controlled ambient vehicles: minimum 20 minutes. 4. Dual-temperature vehicles: each compartment must reach set point before first pallet enters. Dock doors may remain open for a maximum of 7 minutes during cold chain loading unless protected by active air curtain or sealed dock shelter. If loading exceeds 20 minutes, temperature must be checked every 10 minutes.

search.heading: 4.3.2 Temperature excursion procedure
search.snippet: When a Temperature Excursion is detected or suspected: 1. Stop picking, loading or dispatch of affected stock. 2. Place affected stock in Quarantine within 15 minutes. 3. Capture temperature graph, alarm log, location, product batch and time range. 4. Notify Quality within the response time in Table 4.1. 5. Check whether stock was Released Stock at the time of excursion. 6. Determine whether customer notification is required. 7. Record deviation in the quality system. 8. Await written Quality release before stock movement. If the excursion affects Category B chilled pharmaceuticals, then maximum excursion time is 30 minutes — except when lane validation documentation approved by Quality permits a named product-specific exposure limit and the product has not exceeded that validated limit. Stock must not be released based only on visual inspection. A normal-looking pharmaceutical product may still be non-compliant. This rule applies even when the customer requests urgent shipment.

search.heading: 5.3 Route Planning and Load Optimisation
search.snippet: Route planners must use the transport management system for all planned routes exceeding 50 kilometres or involving more than 4 delivery points. Manual route planning is permitted for emergency local moves below 50 kilometres but must be entered retrospectively by end of shift. Routes must consider: 1. Delivery window. 2. Driver hours. 3. Vehicle capacity. 4. Vehicle temperature capability. 5. Low-emission zone restrictions. 6. Toll and ferry costs. 7. Customer unloading constraints. 8. Hazardous materials restrictions. 9. Vehicle height, weight and access limits. If route optimisation reduces cost but increases estimated delay beyond 45 minutes, then customer service approval is required — except when the delay avoids a driver-hours breach, bridge restriction, regulatory road closure or safety risk.

search.heading: 6.2 Personal Protective Equipment
search.snippet: Minimum PPE in operational warehouse zones is high-visibility vest, safety footwear and site ID. Additional PPE applies by zone: |Zone or task|Mandatory PPE| |---|---| |Loading bay|High-visibility vest, safety footwear, gloves where handling pallets| |Forklift operating area|High-visibility vest, safety footwear, pedestrian exclusion compliance| |Cold room below 5°C|Thermal jacket, thermal gloves for exposure above 15 minutes| |Zone or task|Mandatory PPE| |---|---| |Freezer below -15°C|Freezer suit, freezer gloves, face protection for exposure above 10 minutes| |Battery charging|Eye protection, chemical gloves, apron where lead-acid batteries are present| |Hazardous materials handling|PPE stated in safety data sheet and site risk assessment| Failure to wear mandatory PPE is a safety violation. “Zero tolerance” for safety violations does not mean automatic dismissal. It means mandatory investigation within 24 hours, documented corrective action, and disciplinary review where intent, repetition or serious risk is established.

search.heading: 2.1 Delegation of Authority
search.snippet: All spending, commitments, hiring, contracts and asset disposals must comply with Table 2.1. Values are stated in EUR excluding VAT, unless the contract or invoice is legally VAT-inclusive and cannot be separated. Table 2.1 — Delegation of Authority Matrix |Decision Type|Band 1–3 max EUR amount|Band 4–5 max EUR amount|Band 6+ max EUR amount|Board| |---|---|---|---|---| |Capital expenditure|€0|€18,750|€247,500|Above €247,500| |Operating expenditure|€2,950|€28,600|€186,400|Above €186,400| |Contract signing|€0|€24,999|€312,750|Above €312,750| |Headcount approval|€0|1 role up to €54,500 annual cost|6 roles up to €486,000 annual cost|Above 6 roles or €486,000| |IT procurement|€1,200|€15,000|€124,800|Above €124,800| |Fleet acquisition|€0|€41,250|€598,000|Above €598,000| |Lease commitment|€0|€36,800 total term value|€428,500 total term value|Above €428,500| |Marketing spend|€750|€11,400|€76,250|Above €76,250| |Emergency purchase|€6,500|€39,750|€155,000|Above €155,000 or retrospective ratification| |Asset disposal|€500 book value|€12,250 book value|€95,500 book value|Above €95,500| All approvals must be obtained before commitment — except when the purchase is an Emergency Purchase as defined in Section 1.2 and documented within 24 hours under Section 2.2.5. The financial delegation limits in Table 2.1 apply to the total commitment value, not the monthly invoice amount. A 36-month lease at €9,000 per month is a €324,000 lease commitment, subject to Band 6+ approval and possibly Board approval. For contract signing controls, see Section 2.5.

search.heading: 3.5.1 Review timing
search.snippet: A post-incident review must occur within: 1. 5 Working Days for Critical Incidents. 2. 10 Working Days for Major Incidents. 3. 20 Working Days for selected Minor Incidents. 4. 30 Working Days for recurring Observations. The review must include timeline, root cause, failed controls, working controls, customer impact, regulatory exposure, financial exposure, corrective actions, owner, due date and effectiveness check.

search.heading: Expected office attendance
search.snippet:
Expected office attendance

Hybrid employees attend the office a minimum of two days per week. Teams may agree a
fixed anchor day; where they do, attendance on that day takes precedence over the
individual minimum.
